why: Today's tooling, the one review of the typecheck port at abfac52: sent back, two blocking classes. (1) The lock can have two live holders. LocksFile.ts:108-110 removes a .break whose holder is gone with no lock held, and :123 removes .break on the way out whatever it names now. With one breaker killed while it held .break, two live takers C and B can run: C reads the dead .break; B removes it and links its own; C removes B's .break and links its own; both look under their .break, both see the old label stale; B removes it and links its label; C then removes B's live label and links its own. A scratch scenario on the tests' in-memory disk, ordered by Deferred gates, ended with both hold calls returned and no release (vitest passed on the assertion [true, true]); it was deleted after the run. This breaks 0410's rule, one type check at a time across shells, and its 2026-11-15 amendment's 'following Mercurial's repository lock': Mercurial takes the .break lock as a lock instance with timeout=0, so a dead .break is itself broken under its own .break. The plan's line 'that only races if two breakers both died within a few milliseconds' is wrong: one dead breaker is enough. N3's walk kills only holders, never a breaker, so it cannot reach the case. (2) Decision 0567, which covers our tooling (and next/AGENTS.md, which 0033 applies here), says a tagged value is matched and never compared by hand. The new product files compare _tag by hand at LocksFile.ts:19, 104, 108, 117, 168 and 175, Look.ts:84 and Typecheck.ts:69 (NodeModulesFs.ts:20 sits straight inside Effect.catchIf, which the rule skips), and the two new test files do it 16 times. Everything else held: every caller of typecheck.sh left is a record or a history comment; caches.ts reads the buildinfo path from scripts/typecheck.ts; L2 repeats the lead-tooling block's list exactly, plus tea; E1's new body and the until waits in E2, E4 and E6 are tighter than before, not looser; signals are re-raised after the scope closes, since runMain removes its own listeners before the teardown; detached is false; pgrep exits 0 and 1 are listed and anything else refused; a broken node_modules link gives one line and exit 1.
